mainTopic: The end of the סנהדרין's exiles, the תקנה that witnesses go to the court's meeting place, and the nine תקנות of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, including the dispute over the ninth
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing the list of places the סנהדרין moved to, ending in טבריא, the lowest spot, which a פסוק hints at. רבי אלעזר counts six exiles, and רבי יוחנן adds that the redemption will start from that lowest point. A new משנה teaches another תקנה of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: witnesses for the new moon go to the court's meeting place, even if the ראש בית דין is elsewhere. The גמרא tells how אמימר banned a woman who did not follow him to another town. רב אשי challenges him from the משנה, and אמימר answers that the rule applies only to new-moon witnesses, while in money cases the defendant must follow the court. A ברייתא then teaches that כהנים may not go up to the דוכן in sandals, one of nine תקנות of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. The גמרא names the other תקנות, including canceling a גר's duty to set aside money for his birds. The ninth is disputed: רב פפא says כרם רבעי, and רב נחמן בר יצחק says the crimson strip of יום כיפור. Each side defends its view against the other, and רב נחמן בר יצחק's final answer continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The סנהדרין keeps moving from town to town
steps.stepSummary: The list of the סנהדרין's moves continues from יבנה through אושא, שפרעם, בית שערים and ציפורי, ending in טבריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from יבנה to אושא, and from אושא back to יבנה, and from יבנה again to אושא, and from אושא to שפרעם, and from שפרעם to בית שערים, and from בית שערים to ציפורי, and from ציפורי to טבריא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list it began earlier: every place the סנהדרין went to after it left the Temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court went back and forth between יבנה and אושא more than once. That is why the list counts journeys and not only places. After that the court moved through towns in the גליל until it settled in טבריא.

keyTerms.meaning: The town where the סנהדרין moved after the Temple's destruction
A major city in the גליל
The last stop of the סנהדרין

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of a new topic. The list began on the previous עמוד, with the סנהדרין's earliest moves from the Temple. Here we only see its ending.

phrases.english: And from Yavne to Usha, and from Usha back to Yavne,
and from Yavne again to Usha, and from Usha to Shefaram,
and from Shefaram to Beit She'arim,
and from Beit She'arim to Tzippori,
and from Tzippori to Tiberias.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִיַּבְנֶה לְאוּשָׁא, וּמֵאוּשָׁא לְיַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of the סנהדרין's exiles earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סנהדרין's journeys ended in טבריא.

steps.title: טבריא is the lowest, hinted at in a verse
steps.stepSummary: טבריא is lower than all the other places, and a פסוק in ישעיהו hints at this final lowering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And טבריא is lower than all of them, as it says: 'And brought down, you shall speak out of the ground.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that the last stop was physically the lowest, and it brings a פסוק that hints at this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבריא sits deep in the valley of the ירדן. The physical drop matches a spiritual drop: each move took the סנהדרין further down from its place of honor. The פסוק 'וְשָׁפַלְתְּ' (you will be brought low) describes exactly this.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said (introduces a verse)
and you shall be brought low

phrases.english: And Tiberias is lower than all of them,
as it says: 'And brought down, you shall speak out of the ground.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּטְבֶרְיָא עֲמוּקָּה מִכּוּלָּן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural hint for the end point of the list.
steps.raayaObject: That the final exile, to טבריא, was the lowest.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר counts six exiles
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says there were six exiles, and he hints at this from a פסוק that uses six expressions of lowering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: There are six exiles, as it says: 'For He has brought down those who dwell high, the lofty city, laying it low, laying it low to the ground, bringing it to the dust.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר offers a different way to count the exiles: six instead of ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier count of ten counted every trip, including going back and forth. רבי אלעזר counts the places, not each journey. His פסוק has six words of lowering: הֵשַׁח, יַשְׁפִּילֶנָּה, יַשְׁפִּילָהּ, עַד אֶרֶץ, יַגִּיעֶנָּה, עַד עָפָר.

keyTerms.meaning: exile (here, a forced move of the סנהדרין)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says: There are six exiles,
as it says: 'For He has brought down those who dwell high,
the lofty city, laying it low,
laying it low to the ground,
bringing it to the dust.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: שֵׁשׁ גָּלוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second count of the exiles, with a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There were six exiles, matching the six expressions of lowering in the פסוק.

steps.title: Redemption will begin from the lowest point
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the future redemption will start from the lowest place the סנהדרין reached.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: And from there they are destined to be redeemed, as it says: 'Shake yourself from the dust, arise, sit.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן ends the topic on a hopeful note: the place where the people sank lowest is where the redemption will begin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous פסוק ended with 'עַד עָפָר', down to the dust. רבי יוחנן answers with a פסוק that begins 'הִתְנַעֲרִי מֵעָפָר', shake yourself from the dust. The same word links the lowest point of the descent to the start of the rise.
steps.whatToRemember: The סנהדרין went down step by step to טבריא, the lowest place. From that lowest point, the redemption will rise up.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And from there they are destined to be redeemed,
as it says: 'Shake yourself from the dust, arise, sit.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּמִשָּׁם עֲתִידִין לִיגָּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the topic of the exiles with a promise of redemption.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The redemption will begin from the lowest place of the exile.

steps.title: Witnesses go to the court's meeting place
steps.stepSummary: The משנה reports another תקנה of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: witnesses for the new moon go to where the court meets, even if the ראש בית דין is elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי יהושע בן קרחה said: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי also instituted this: even if the head of the court is in some other place, the witnesses should go only to the place where the court gathers.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It adds one more תקנה made by רבן יוחנן בן זכאי after the Temple was destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think witnesses must go wherever the ראש בית דין is, since he is the one who says 'מקודש'. The תקנה says no: the witnesses go to the court's set meeting place. The court there can sanctify the month without him.

keyTerms.meaning: the place where the court gathers

steps.whyThisMatters: The authority to act belongs to the court as a body in its set place, not to one leader personally. רב אשי will use exactly this point in the story that follows.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said:

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד זֹאת הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
phrases.english: And this too Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ רֹאשׁ בֵּית דִּין בְּכׇל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: that even if the head of the court is in any other place,
the witnesses should not go
anywhere except to the place where the court gathers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד זֹאת הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses go only to the court's meeting place, even when the ראש בית דין is elsewhere.

steps.title: אמימר bans a woman who did not follow him
steps.stepSummary: A woman was summoned to אמימר's court in נהרדעא. אמימר traveled to מחוזא, she did not follow him there, and he wrote a document of excommunication against her.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: There was a certain woman who was summoned to judgment before אמימר in נהרדעא. אמימר went to מחוזא, and she did not go after him. He wrote a document of excommunication against her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up a challenge based on our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר treated her refusal to follow him as contempt of court, and he issued a פתיחא, a written ban. The question underneath is whether a case follows the judge personally or stays at the court's set location.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
A certain woman was summoned to judgment
before Ameimar in Nehardea.
Ameimar went to Mechoza,
and she did not go after him.
He wrote a document of excommunication against her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהִיא אִיתְּתָא דְּאַזְמְנוּהָ לְדִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical case that connects to the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אמימר placed a ban on a litigant who would not follow him to another town.

steps.title: רב אשי challenges אמימר from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks אמימר how he could ban her, since the משנה says people go to the court's place and not after the ראש בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: But didn't we learn: Even if the head of the court is in any other place, the witnesses should go only to the place where the court gathers!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges אמימר's action by quoting our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the משנה, people go to the court's fixed location, not to wherever the head judge travels. The woman was summoned in נהרדעא, so she was right to stay there. That means אמימר should not have banned her.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't we learn (introduces a challenge from a source)

steps.confusionAlert: The words quoted here are the same words as the משנה in step 5. The גמרא is not repeating them by accident. It quotes them on purpose to attack אמימר's ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ רֹאשׁ בֵּית דִּין בְּכׇל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: Even if the head of the court is in any other place,
the witnesses should not go
anywhere except to the place where the court gathers!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר, וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the action described in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ban on the woman for not following him to מחוזא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says people go to the court's fixed place, not to wherever the head judge is. So the woman had no duty to follow אמימר, and banning her seems wrong.

steps.title: אמימר explains why money cases are different
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that the rule about going to the court's place applies only to עדות החודש. In money cases, the defendant must follow the court.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That rule applies only to new-moon testimony. Otherwise you would be tripping up the witnesses for the future. But here, in a money case, 'the borrower is a servant to the lender.'
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר defends his ban on the woman. He says the משנה's rule was made only for new-moon witnesses, not for people being sued in court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New-moon witnesses are doing the community a favor. If they had to chase the ראש בית דין around, they might not bother coming next time, so they go to the fixed meeting place. In a money case, the defendant is the one who owes, so like a borrower to a lender, he must go where the court is.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only to...): a phrase that limits a rule to a specific case
Testimony that the new moon was seen
You trip them up, meaning you discourage them
For the future, here meaning next time
The borrower is a servant to the lender (משלי כב:ז)

steps.confusionAlert: Here לעתיד לבא does not mean the messianic era. It simply means future occasions, the next time witnesses might need to come.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a practical principle: in monetary disputes, the defendant must come to wherever the court sits.

phrases.english: He (Ameimar) said to him (Rav Ashi):
These words apply only to new-moon testimony,
because if so (if they had to follow the head of court), you would be found
tripping them up for the future.
phrases.notes: They might not come to testify next time.

phrases.english: But here (a money case),
'The borrower is a servant to the lender.'
phrases.notes: The defendant must go where the court is.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה הני מילי לענין עדות החדש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge from step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source: the משנה's rule is restricted to עדות החודש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אשי thought the משנה's rule (go to the court's place, not after the ראש בית דין) applies to all cases
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is special to new-moon witnesses so they won't be discouraged. In money cases the defendant must follow the court, so the ban was justified.

steps.title: No sandals on the platform, one of nine enactments
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that כהנים may not go up to the דוכן in sandals. This is one of nine תקנות of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: six in this פרק and one in the first פרק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: כהנים are not allowed to go up to the platform in their sandals. This is one of the nine enactments that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made. Six are in this chapter and one is in the first chapter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes a ברייתא about כהנים and sandals, then starts counting all of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our פרק already mentioned several of his תקנות, and this ברייתא adds the sandals rule. It also gives a total of nine, which sets up the גמרא to identify the last two.

keyTerms.meaning: The platform where כהנים stand to give ברכת כהנים

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice that כהנים remove their shoes before ברכת כהנים.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught (in a baraita):
Kohanim are not permitted
to go up in their sandals to the platform,
and this is one of nine enactments
that Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted.
Six are in this chapter,
phrases.notes: שופר on שבת in יבנה, לולב all seven days, חדש forbidden all day of the waving, new-moon testimony accepted all day, witnesses go to the meeting place, and no sandals for כהנים.

phrases.english: and one is in the first chapter.
phrases.notes: Witnesses may break שבת only for ניסן and תשרי.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנו רבנן אין כהנים רשאין לעלות בסנדליהן לדוכן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: listing רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactments
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים may not go up to the דוכן in sandals. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made nine תקנות: six in this פרק and one in the first.

steps.title: The eighth enactment: a convert's money for his birds
steps.stepSummary: The eighth תקנה is about a גר who is told to set aside money for his bird offering. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי canceled this out of fear of a mishap.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another one, as a ברייתא teaches: A convert who converts nowadays must set aside a quarter coin for his pair of birds. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said: רבן יוחנן already took a vote and canceled it, because of the risk of a mishap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the eighth enactment. Here the enactment is actually a cancellation of an older rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר must bring a bird offering. After the בית המקדש was destroyed, he was told to set aside money for it for when it is rebuilt. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי canceled this, because someone might accidentally use the holy money and commit מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter (a coin amount, enough for the birds)
His 'nest': his pair of bird offerings
A mishap, here meaning the risk of misusing holy money

steps.confusionAlert: The first part of the ברייתא gives the old rule (set money aside). רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactment is the cancellation of that rule.

phrases.english: And the other one is as taught in a baraita:
A convert who converts nowadays (without a Temple)
must set aside a quarter coin for his pair of birds.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָר נִמְנָה עָלֶיהָ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן וּבִיטְּלָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan already took a vote on it and canceled it,
because of the risk of a mishap.
phrases.notes: Someone might use the consecrated money by mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואידך דתניא גר שנתגייר בזמן הזה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the eighth of the nine תקנות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי canceled the requirement for a גר to set aside money for his bird offering, because of the risk of misusing holy money.

steps.title: The ninth enactment is disputed
steps.stepSummary: The ninth תקנה is disputed. רב פפא says it is about כרם רבעי, and רב נחמן בר יצחק says it is about the crimson strip.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the last one is a dispute between רב פפא and רב נחמן בר יצחק. רב פפא said: a fourth-year vineyard. רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the strip of crimson wool.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to name the ninth and final enactment, but two אמוראים disagree about what it was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא says it concerned the fruit of a fourth-year vineyard. It is commonly explained that after the destruction, the duty to bring that fruit to ירושלים was dropped. רב נחמן בר יצחק says it concerned the crimson wool strip used on יום כיפור, which turned white as a sign of forgiveness. The total stays nine, but the ninth item is in dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: A vineyard in its fourth year, whose fruit has special holiness
A strip of crimson wool (used on יום כיפור)

steps.whatToRemember: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made nine תקנות: six in our פרק (including no sandals for כהנים), one in the first פרק, one about the גר's birds, and a ninth disputed between כרם רבעי and the crimson strip.

phrases.english: And the other one is a dispute

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב פָּפָּא וְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק.
phrases.english: between Rav Pappa and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak.
Rav Pappa said: a fourth-year vineyard.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: לָשׁוֹן שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: the strip of crimson wool.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואידך פלוגתא דרב פפא ורב נחמן בר יצחק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the count of nine by naming the disputed ninth תקנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ninth תקנה is either about כרם רבעי (רב פפא) or about the crimson strip (רב נחמן בר יצחק).

steps.title: The original rule: fruit near Jerusalem must be brought there
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the ninth תקנה concerns כרם רבעי. He cites the old rule that such fruit within a day's walk of ירושלים had to be brought there as fruit, and he lists the boundaries.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the ninth תקנה is about כרם רבעי. As a ברייתא teaches: fruit of a fourth-year vineyard would be brought up to ירושלים if it grew within a day's walk in any direction. These were the borders: אילת in the north, עקרבת in the south, לוד in the west, and the ירדן in the east.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains רב פפא's view by showing the earlier rule that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי later canceled. This sets up the rest of this passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally כרם רבעי fruit can be redeemed for money, and the money is spent in ירושלים. This source adds a special rule: if the vineyard was within a day's walk of ירושלים, you could not redeem it. You had to bring the actual grapes.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a vineyard in its fourth year. It is eaten in ירושלים like מעשר שני.
Second tithe. It is eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money that is spent there.

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not a new opinion. It is the old rule that existed BEFORE the תקנה. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ninth תקנה was to cancel this rule.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: a fourth-year vineyard,
phrases.notes: This is the ninth תקנה according to him.

phrases.english: as it is taught: a fourth-year vineyard
phrases.notes: The source for the original rule.

phrases.english: would go up to Jerusalem
phrases.notes: The actual fruit had to be brought there.

phrases.english: from a day's walk in every direction,
and this is its boundary:

phrases.aramaic: אֵילַת מִן הַצָּפוֹן, וְעַקְרַבַּת מִן הַדָּרוֹם,
phrases.english: Eilat to the north, and Akrabat to the south,

phrases.aramaic: לוֹד מִן הַמַּעֲרָב, וְיַרְדֵּן מִן הַמִּזְרָח.
phrases.english: Lod to the west, and the Jordan to the east.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רב פפא's one-line view from step 11 by quoting the original rule that the תקנה changed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before the תקנה, כרם רבעי growing within a day's walk of ירושלים had to be brought there as actual fruit.

steps.title: The reason: to fill Jerusalem's markets with fruit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the purpose of the rule was to decorate the markets of ירושלים with fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said, and some say it was רבה בר עולא, in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is the reason for this rule? To decorate the markets of ירושלים with fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind the rule from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the nearby farmers had to bring real grapes, ירושלים was always full of fresh fruit. The reason is tied to a living, busy ירושלים. That sets up why the rule could be canceled once ירושלים was destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say. It introduces another version of who said it.

steps.whyThisMatters: Once you know the reason, you can see why the rule could lapse. With the בית המקדש destroyed, there was no longer a point in decorating ירושלים's markets.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר עוּלָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא
phrases.english: And Ulla said, and some say Rabba bar Ulla,
phrases.notes: Two versions of who reported it.

phrases.english: said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
What is the reason?
In order to adorn the markets of Jerusalem with fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר עוּלָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מָה טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the purpose of the rule quoted in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule existed to make sure ירושלים's markets were full of fruit.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's vineyard near Lod
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that רבי אליעזר had a כרם רבעי east of לוד, inside the zone. He wanted to make it ownerless for the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר had a fourth-year vineyard east of לוד, next to the village of כפר טבי. רבי אליעזר wanted to make it ownerless for the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story as proof that the old rule was canceled. This step only sets up the case; the proof comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: East of לוד is inside the zone, so by the old rule the grapes had to be brought to ירושלים. After the חורבן, רבי אליעזר could not easily do that. So he planned to give up ownership in favor of the poor, for whom the trip would be worthwhile.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught. It introduces a ברייתא.
A village east of לוד, inside the zone.

phrases.english: And it was taught: a fourth-year vineyard belonged
to Rabbi Eliezer, to the east of Lod
phrases.notes: Between לוד and ירושלים, so inside the border.

phrases.english: next to the village of Tavi,
and Rabbi Eliezer wanted
to make it ownerless for the poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי הָיָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case in which the rule from steps 12-13 applied.
steps.raayaObject: That the rule requiring the actual fruit to be brought was canceled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about רבי אליעזר's כרם רבעי near לוד.

steps.title: The students: the rule was already voted away
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's students tell him not to bother, because his colleagues already voted and permitted the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students said to him: רבי, your colleagues already took a vote on this and permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the proof. The students report that the old requirement was officially canceled by a vote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permitted means the fruit near ירושלים may now be redeemed like any other כרם רבעי. There is no need to haul it to ירושלים. The rule's purpose was to adorn ירושלים, and that purpose no longer applied after the חורבן, so the Sages removed it.

phrases.english: His students said to him: Our teacher,
your colleagues have already voted on it
and permitted it.
phrases.notes: It may be redeemed. There is no need to bring the fruit itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: רַבִּי, כְּבָר נִמְנוּ חֲבֵרֶיךָ עָלָיו וְהִתִּירוּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story from step 14 with the students' answer.
steps.raayaObject: That the old requirement was officially canceled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The students' report of a vote by רבי אליעזר's colleagues.

steps.title: The colleague who canceled it was רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the colleagues were and answers that it was רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. This confirms that the cancellation was his תקנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are 'your colleagues'? רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies who led the vote, and that finishes the proof for רב פפא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By naming רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, the גמרא presents the proof for רב פפא: canceling the כרם רבעי rule was one of his תקנות, so it can be the ninth. This identification is challenged later, in step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: The leader after the חורבן, who made the תקנות in this פרק.

steps.confusionAlert: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was actually רבי אליעזר's teacher, yet the students call him a 'colleague.' This wording is exactly what the two אמוראים argue about: רב נחמן בר יצחק says it rules out רבן יוחנן בן זכאי (step 20), and רב פפא explains it as respectful speech (step 21).
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, the ninth תקנה was canceling the requirement to bring כרם רבעי near ירושלים as actual fruit. The rule's purpose was to fill ירושלים's markets, and that no longer applied after the חורבן. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי led the vote.

phrases.english: Who are 'your colleagues'?
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן חֲבֵרֶיךָ — רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the colleagues in step 15, tying the story back to רב פפא's claim in step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Canceling the כרם רבעי requirement was a תקנה of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, which supports רב פפא's identification of the ninth תקנה.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the ninth enactment was the crimson strip
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the ninth תקנה concerned the לשון של זהורית. He cites a ברייתא: at first the strip hung outside the אולם, and later the חכמים moved it inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It was the crimson strip. As a ברייתא teaches: At first they tied a crimson strip on the outside of the doorway of the אולם. If it turned white, people were happy. If it did not, they were sad. So the Sages enacted that it be tied on the inside of the doorway.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a different answer from רב פפא about what the ninth תקנה was. He backs it up with a ברייתא about the crimson strip of יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור the crimson strip turning white was a sign that the sins were forgiven. When it did not turn white, the whole public became sad. So the חכמים moved the strip inside the doorway, where fewer people could see it.

keyTerms.meaning: A strip of crimson-dyed wool used on יום כיפור.
The entrance hall of the בית המקדש.
It turned white, a sign of forgiveness.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It was the strip of crimson wool.
phrases.notes: This is his answer to which enactment was the ninth.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
At first they would tie
a strip of crimson wool
on the doorway of the Entrance Hall, on the outside.
If it turned white, they would rejoice;
if it did not turn white, they would be sad.
So they enacted that they should tie it
on the doorway of the Entrance Hall, on the inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: לָשׁוֹן שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative to רב פפא's identification of the ninth תקנה (steps 12-16).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ninth תקנה concerned the placement of the לשון של זהורית.

steps.title: People still peeked, so the strip was moved to the rock and the goat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: people still peeked at the strip inside. So the חכמים had it tied half to the rock and half between the horns of the שעיר המשתלח, far from the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: But people would still peek and see. If it turned white, they were happy. If it did not, they were sad. So the Sages enacted that half the strip be tied to the rock and half between the horns of the goat sent away.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the story. This last change is the תקנה that רב נחמן בר יצחק says was the ninth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the strip inside did not solve the problem, because people still peeked. The final solution moved the strip out to the desert, at the cliff where the goat was sent. Nobody in ירושלים could see it during יום כיפור, so no one would be upset.

keyTerms.meaning: The rock or cliff in the desert where the goat was sent.
The goat sent away to עזאזל on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: But they would still peek and see it.
If it turned white, they would rejoice;
if it did not turn white, they would be sad.
So they enacted that they should tie it
half of it to the rock

phrases.aramaic: וְחֶצְיוֹ בֵּין קַרְנָיו שֶׁל שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ.
phrases.english: and half of it between the horns of the scapegoat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲדַיִין הָיוּ מְצִיצִין וְרוֹאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא cited in step 17 and reaches the final תקנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that the ninth תקנה involved the crimson strip.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא describing the two-stage relocation of the strip.

steps.title: Why didn't רב נחמן בר יצחק agree with רב פפא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reason רב נחמן בר יצחק had for not accepting רב פפא's answer about כרם רבעי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק, what is the reason he did not say like רב פפא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now compares the two opinions. This question sets up the next step, which gives רב נחמן בר יצחק's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא had a ברייתא that seemed to show רבן יוחנן בן זכאי canceled the כרם רבעי rule (step 16). So the גמרא wants to know what was wrong with that proof in רב נחמן בר יצחק's eyes.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב פָּפָּא?
phrases.english: what is the reason he did not say like Rav Pappa?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from presenting the two views to analyzing why each rejected the other.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The weakness רב נחמן בר יצחק saw in רב פפא's proof.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was רבי אליעזר's teacher, not his colleague
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק would say that the ברייתא calls the people who voted רבי אליעזר's 'colleagues.' But רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was his teacher, so the ברייתא cannot be about him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: If you think it was רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, was he רבי אליעזר's colleague? He was his teacher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב נחמן בר יצחק's reason. The wording 'your colleagues' does not fit רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 the students said 'your colleagues voted.' A colleague is an equal. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was רבי אליעזר's רבי, so the ברייתא must be talking about other people, and רב פפא's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind, meaning 'if you think that'.

phrases.english: He would say to you:

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
phrases.english: If it enters your mind that it was Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,
was he Rabbi Eliezer's colleague?
He was his teacher!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by attacking the wording of רב פפא's ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'colleagues' cannot describe רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, who was רבי אליעזר's teacher.

steps.title: רב פפא: students would not say 'your teacher' to their own teacher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב פפא would answer. He would say the students called רבן יוחנן בן זכאי 'your colleagues' out of respect, because it is not proper to say 'your teacher' to one's own teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רב פפא? Since they were students, it is not proper manners to say to one's teacher 'your teacher.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends his proof. The word 'colleagues' was just a polite way of speaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students were speaking to their own רבי, רבי אליעזר. Saying 'your teacher permitted it' would make their רבי sound small in front of them. So they chose the respectful word 'colleagues,' even though they meant רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? How would he answer?

phrases.english: And the other one (Rav Pappa)?
Since they were students,
it is not proper conduct
to say to one's teacher, 'your teacher.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? כֵּיוָן דְּתַלְמִידִים הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב פפא against the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of wording as respectful speech.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Colleagues' must literally mean equals, so it cannot mean רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Colleagues' was a respectful expression and can refer to רבי אליעזר's teacher.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן בר יצחק reads 'colleagues' literally. רב פפא says it was said out of respect, so רבן יוחנן בן זכאי can still be the one who voted.

steps.title: Why didn't רב פפא agree with רב נחמן בר יצחק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks the reverse: why did רב פפא not accept the crimson-strip answer?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא, what is the reason he did not say like רב נחמן בר יצחק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the comparison around. This sets up רב פפא's reason in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the question is what problem רב פפא saw in linking the crimson-strip תקנה to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa, what is the reason

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר כְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק?
phrases.english: he did not say like Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב פָּפָּא מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 19 in the other direction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רב פפא's objection to the crimson-strip answer.

steps.title: Was there even a crimson strip miracle in רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's time?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא would say that in רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's days the crimson strip was no longer relevant. So he could not have made a תקנה about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: If you think it was רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, in the days of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was there a crimson strip?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב פפא's reason. The timing does not work for the crimson-strip answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תקנה about hiding whether the strip turned white only makes sense if the strip sometimes did turn white. רב פפא claims this miracle no longer happened in רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's time. The proof for this comes next.

phrases.english: He would say to you:

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי —
phrases.english: If it enters your mind that it was Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,
in the days of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
was there a crimson strip?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי — בִּימֵי רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי מִי הֲוָה לָשׁוֹן שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 with a historical-timing objection.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The crimson-strip situation did not exist in רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's time, so the תקנה cannot be his.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's 120 years: business, learning, teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי lived 120 years. He spent 40 in business, 40 learning, and 40 teaching. This begins the proof about the timing, which is completed next.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is taught in a ברייתא: All the years of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי were 120. Forty years he was in business, forty years he learned, forty years he taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to prove רב פפא's timing claim by laying out the stages of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's life. Step 25 completes the proof by connecting these years to the crimson strip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's period of leadership, his 40 years of teaching, can be dated. The גמרא will show that during those years the strip no longer turned white. So a תקנה about hiding the strip would have had no purpose then.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? It introduces a source used as proof.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the proof is complete here. The 120-year breakdown alone does not yet mention the crimson strip. The link comes in step 25.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: All the years of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
were one hundred and twenty years.
Forty years he engaged in business,
forty years he studied,
forty years he taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: כׇּל שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source-based proof for רב פפא's timing objection in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that the crimson-strip issue did not exist in רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's era.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא dividing רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's 120 years into three 40-year periods. It is completed next.

steps.title: The crimson strip stopped working forty years before the Temple fell
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the crimson strip stopped turning white forty years before the חורבן. A משנה shows that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's leadership began after the חורבן. So he could not have made a תקנה about the strip as a leader.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches: for the forty years before the Temple was destroyed, the crimson strip did not turn white. Instead, it turned red. And our משנה teaches: once the Temple was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made his תקנות. This shows the strip was no longer relevant in his time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof that began in Step 24. It brings one more ברייתא and one משנה to show that the crimson strip was already irrelevant when רבן יוחנן בן זכאי became a leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 split his 120 years into three blocks of forty. The משנה shows that his teaching and leading years began at the חורבן. The ברייתא says the strip had already stopped turning white forty years before the חורבן. So during his entire leadership, there was nothing about the strip that needed a תקנה. This supports רב פפא's rejection of the crimson-strip answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The strip of crimson wool, which would turn white as a sign that Israel's sins were forgiven on יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
And we learned in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא is saying רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was not alive forty years before the חורבן. He was alive, but he was still in his learning years then, not a leader who makes תקנות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This timing proof is the whole reason רב פפא rejects רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that the ninth תקנה was about the crimson strip.

phrases.english: And it was taught in a baraita: forty years
before the Temple was destroyed
the strip of crimson wool did not
turn white; rather, it turned red.
phrases.notes: The sign of forgiveness stopped appearing.

phrases.english: And we learned in the Mishnah: from when the Temple was destroyed
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted his ordinances!
phrases.notes: So his leadership years began at the destruction, after the strip had already stopped working.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה קוֹדֶם שֶׁנֶּחֱרַב הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the timing proof that began with the 120-year ברייתא in Step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that in רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's days the crimson strip was no longer relevant
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the strip turning red for forty years before the חורבן, together with the משנה that he made his תקנות after the חורבן

steps.title: He suggested the idea while still a student
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב נחמן בר יצחק would answer the timing proof. He says the crimson-strip idea came from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי during his forty learning years. He was then a student sitting before his teacher, and the Sages accepted his reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion, how does he answer? During those forty years that he was learning, he was a student sitting before his teacher. He said something, and his reasoning made sense to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב נחמן בר יצחק deals with רב פפא's timing proof. It answers that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי did not need to be a leader to have his idea adopted. The sentence continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא assumed that only a leader could make a תקנה. רב נחמן בר יצחק says that even as a student, during his learning years when the strip was still an issue, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי could suggest an idea. The Sages found his reasoning convincing and adopted it. So the timing problem goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning: how would the other opinion answer?
A student sitting before his teacher, someone still learning and not yet a leader
And his reasoning made sense, so it was accepted

steps.confusionAlert: Here, וְאִידַּךְ refers to רב נחמן בר יצחק, the opinion that the ninth תקנה was about the crimson strip. It is not רב פפא.

phrases.english: And the other (how would he answer)?
phrases.notes: This refers to רב נחמן בר יצחק.

phrases.english: During those forty years that he studied,
he was a student sitting before his teacher,
and he said a matter (suggested this ordinance),
and his reasoning made sense (to the Sages).
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ: אוֹתָם אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה דְּלָמַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב נחמן בר יצחק's crimson-strip reading against the timing proof completed in Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-timing the event: the idea was proposed during his student years, not his leadership years
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the strip stopped turning white before רבן יוחנן בן זכאי became a leader, he could not have made a תקנה about it.
steps.terutzMaskana: He suggested the idea as a student during his learning years, while the strip was still relevant, and the Sages adopted it because his reasoning was convincing.
